title: Redwood Optimize Walkthrough - Batching & KV Cache Cost Model
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Atlas Financial through Redwood Optimize recommendations focusing on batching strategies and prefix/KV caching. Discussed cost model tradeoffs, expected latency impact, and pilot next steps. Action: send customized cost spreadsheet, schedule benchmarking run in Dedicated/Hosted comparison, share security brief.
next_steps: Samir to share tailored cost model spreadsheet and example configs by 2026-04-18
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run (Atlas test corpus) week of 2026-04-20 (SE + Atlas SRE)
Share SOC2/Security one-pager and KMS integration doc
Follow-up call to review benchmark results and pilot contract
action_items: Samir: send tailored cost model spreadsheet by 2026-04-18
Jules: prepare benchmark run checklist and infra playbook by 2026-04-17
Maya: provide 50 representative prompts and traffic profile by 2026-04-16
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. We'll do a 45-ish minute walkthrough of Optimize recommendations focused on batching and KV/prefix cache and then leave time for Q&A. Jules, you want to kick off?

[00:18] Jules (Redwood SE): Yeah sorry, hi everybody. I'm Jules here, I'm the solutions engineer. Quick agenda: a brief recap of Atlas' current setup that Maya shared, then demo of Optimize console suggestions, deep dive into batching strategies, how our KV/prefix cache works and cost-model examples.

[00:35] Maya (Atlas): Hey hi, thanks. Yep we're excited, got Rajiv and Lena here too; we're trying to control token costs for our customer-facing chat while keeping sub-400ms p99 latency. We're currently on hosted endpoints with mixed traffic and some bursts.

[00:52] Rajiv (Atlas): Also curious about Dedicated vs staying hosted for predictable throughput; and how cache invalidation handles regulatory PII redaction flows.

[01:05] Jules: Good callouts. Quick confirm: your traffic today avg QPS is ~120 with 30-40% peaks to 300 QPS during market open?

[01:12] Maya: That's correct, monthly active users ~200k. Typical prompt lengths 80-150 tokens, responses 120-300 tokens.

[01:28] Samir: Ok great. So first slide — Optimize recommendations surface: we analyze your traffic heatmap and suggest batching window, target batch size, and where prefix caching yields the most hit-rate. For Atlas with lots of repeated prefixes (account IDs, legal boilerplate) prefix/KV cache should be high impact.

[01:50] [Demo noise: screen share starts]

[02:10] Jules: Here's the Optimize console — sample suggestions for batching: 40ms batching window avg with adaptive backpressure. That translates to batching of 6-12 requests per micro-batch at your current QPS. Note: batching reduces per-token GPU overhead but adds tail latency.

[02:35] Maya: When you say 40ms window, does that add to our p95/p99? We're sensitive at p99 < 400ms.

[02:44] Jules: We typically target latency SLOs with adaptive policies. For example, we suggested a micro-batch window of 40ms with a max micro-batch of 16; in our sim this increased p99 by ~20-35ms but reduced cost per token by about 22% for your token distribution. Those are estimates — we'd run a benchmark on your corpus to validate.

[03:10] Rajiv: Okay that seems promising. What about KV cache?

[03:16] Jules: KV/prefix cache works two ways: a short prefix-KV cache in the serving layer for recent tokens and a longer-lived application-level KV cache keyed by prefix hash. For Atlas we saw many repeated prompts with same financial context prefixes — that could yield hit rates of 35-55% depending on deduplication. Hit-rate directly maps to lower per-request decoding cost.

[03:45] Lena (Atlas SRE): How do you handle cache consistency when we rotate keys or redact? We have strict compliance workflows.

[03:53] Jules: We have cache invalidation hooks — you can trigger namespace-level invalidations via API and we can integrate with your revocation/KMS events. Also we support TTLs and versioned prefixes for safe rollouts. For PII flows we recommend application-level policy to avoid caching sensitive outputs; Redwood supports tag-based exclusion.

[04:20] Samir: Note too that Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and reserved GPU capacity which is helpful for heavy burst consistency. Hosted with Optimize can still deliver caching/ batching benefits but you may see more variability if the routing tier shifts models.

[04:38] Maya: For cost modeling, do you have an example showing token savings vs. latency tradeoffs?

[04:45] Jules: Yep let's switch to the cost model tab.

[04:52] [05:00] Jules: So here's a simple model: baseline hosted no-batching, no-cache cost X per 1M tokens. When we enable batching (40ms), we reduce GPU overhead which lowers cost by Y%; adding KV cache with 40% hit-rate reduces decode token count proportionally. Combined effects compound — in our Atlas example we model a 30-40% reduction in total cost for chat workloads. Crucially, the model factors in hit-rate, average response length, and batching efficiency.

[05:34] Maya: Can you share the underlying assumptions? Like tokens counted, model variant, quantization level?

[05:41] Jules: Absolutely. For this run we assumed the standard open-llm variant you're using (quant 8-bit) on A100 equivalent on Dedicated; hosted uses our curated runtime with auto-quant profiles. Tokens: we used 140 tokens out, 100 tokens in avg. Hit-rate set at 40% then varied between 20-60% sensitivity.

[06:02] Rajiv: Any pitfalls where caching actually increases cost?

[06:07] Jules: Yes — if your requests are highly unique or if cache miss penalty is high due to extra KV lookup latency causing retries and smaller effective batch sizes. Also cold cache warmup can add overhead. Our model flags scenarios with <10% predicted hit-rate where caching adds complexity with little benefit.

[06:28] Maya: What about multi-tenant concerns? We don't want one customer's pattern to contaminate another's cache.

[06:34] Jules: We namespace caches per-tenant by default in Hosted; Dedicated gives you tenant isolation at infra level as well. For privacy we also support encryption-at-rest for cache shards and RBAC-controlled access.

[06:48] [08:00] Jules: Demo: I'll show a micro-batch trace. You can see enter: three requests collected at 43ms window, batch size 9, KV cache looked up prefix hash and returned hits for two requests; decode tokens reduced from 3x120 to 1x120+2x10 (cached continuations). That's where we get big reductions.

[08:32] Tommy (Atlas PM): Quick Q: does the cache store model hidden states or only token-level continuations?

[08:38] Jules: Good question — we store prefix continuations and compressed KV entries that map to decoder states, not raw hidden tensors exposed to customers. We use a compact representation optimized for lookup and reconstruction inside the runtime. This is an internal detail but we provide guarantees about not storing raw PII and options to exclude keys.

[09:04] Maya: For the benchmark, can Redwood run our test corpus in both Hosted and Dedicated configurations? We want apples-to-apples.

[09:12] Samir: Yes we can set up a benchmark run. Jules will run a 2-hour test with your corpus on both modes and return a results sheet with p50/p95/p99, token counts, and cost breakdown. That's part of the next steps.

[09:28] [11:00] Rajiv: On the configs — what about batching timeouts for interactive chat vs background rerank jobs?

[11:08] Jules: We recommend per-route policies. Interactive chat routes get aggressive latency SLOs: micro-batch window 25-40ms, max batch 8-12. Background rerank/embedding routes can use 100-200ms windows and much larger batches for better efficiency. Optimize suggests per-route presets you can accept or tweak.

[11:36] Maya: How does caching interact with function/tool calling — we use tool calls intermittently.

[11:44] Jules: Tool outputs are excluded from prefix cache by default unless you mark them as deterministic and safe. For function calling we recommend caching upstream tool responses rather than model outputs.

[12:00] [13:00] Samir: Switching to pricing specifics: the cost model spreadsheet I'll send has line items: baseline compute, decode tokens, memory/ops, network egress, and cache storage. For Atlas's scale we estimate cache storage negligible relative to compute savings.

[13:22] Lena: Storage is fine, but we're worried about hot-shard traffic — any mitigation?

[13:28] Jules: We shard cache keys using consistent hashing and can add replication for hot keys. Also burst spillover to fallback model variant is supported via routing policies to avoid overloads.

[13:46] Maya: Security ask: can we bring our own KMS?

[13:51] Samir: Yes BYOK via customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private and Dedicated; Hosted supports customer KMS integration for encrypting cache and logs in many cases. We'll include the integration doc.

[14:10] [15:00] Jules: Now a short deep dive into hit-rate estimation. Our recommenders use fingerprinting of prefixes + LRU/TTL modeling on your observed traffic, then we simulate hit-rate given various dedupe thresholds. For financial templates like \"account summary for X\" we usually see high prefix collision.

[15:40] Maya: If we change phrasing or templates often will that reduce hit-rate?

[15:45] Jules: Slightly, yes. We recommend normalizing templates and using light canonicalization (strip IDs, normalize dates) before hashing prefixes to lift hit-rate. That can be automated in your app layer or we can provide a small sanitizer to run as a shim.

[16:05] Rajiv: How about instrumentation? We need metrics to prove production savings.

[16:10] Jules: Redwood Console exposes per-route token counts, cache hit/miss rates, batch size distributions, and per-token cost breakdowns. We also export traces to your existing telemetry via OTLP and have dashboards you can import.

[16:28] Maya: Perfect. A question on TTLs — how long do you recommend keeping prefix entries?

[16:33] Jules: Depends on churn. For customer-facing chat maybe 5-30 minutes for short-lived contexts, for stable templates up to hours. We tune based on hit-rate and memory footprint.

[16:50] [18:00] Tommy: Any code examples for SDK calls to set per-route caching rules?

[18:06] Jules: Yes — I'll paste a short snippet in the follow-up. But in the console you can set per-route policies with GUI or via API; fields: micro_batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, cache_policy (ttl, include_regex, exclude_tags).

[18:28] Maya: One more on latencies — do you have benchmarks for p99 with batching + cache on A100 vs L4?

[18:36] Jules: We do. Typically A100 yields lower decode latency for large models; L4-style GPUs are more cost-effective per token for quantized models but can have higher p99. We'll include GPU-specific rows in the spreadsheet.

[19:00] [21:00] Samir: Time check — 30 minutes left; open to Q&A but wanted to cover the pilot plan. Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot with carve-out Dedicated slice or hosted pilot (a/b), run benchmarks, measure savings, then propose a commit if results match targets.

[21:32] Rajiv: We'd prefer a staged pilot: start hosted pilot to validate hit-rate and batching config, then move to Dedicated if stable.

[21:44] Samir: Totally reasonable. We can do hosted first. Our legal/finance teams will propose pilot terms — typical pilot includes limited credits and a simple SLA for the benchmark window.

[22:05] Maya: Any security docs we can review before pilot?

[22:10] Samir: Yes SOC2, ISO, KMS integration and data handling papers — will attach.

[22:26] [24:00] Jules: Quick live example of cost sensitivity: changing hit-rate from 20% -> 50% shifts overall cost by ~18% in our model. You can see a table here with sensitivity to avg response length, which is why we asked for your 50 prompts.

[24:40] Maya: Ok that's helpful. If we want to tune caching more aggressively do you recommend more app-level normalization or rely on Redwood's dedupe heuristics?

[24:47] Jules: A combo: app normalization yields the biggest lift quickly; we'll tune heuristics in the runtime to capture additional collisions.

[25:05] Rajiv: Are there cases where batching causes user-visible artifacts like concatenated responses or partial outputs?

[25:12] Jules: No concatenation artifacts — the runtime demultiplexes results. Partial outputs only happen if a preempt occurs; we recommend graceful timeouts and fallback policies.

[25:36] [27:00] Lena: Can we control eviction priority so some prefixes never evict?

[27:06] Jules: Yes we support pinning keys or using higher priority tiers for hot prefixes — but that increases memory footprint and cost. It's configurable per-namespace.

[27:30] Maya: Any red flags you've seen in other financial customers?

[27:34] Jules: Main issues are not normalizing templates (low hit-rate), mis-scoped TTLs, and not excluding sensitive outputs. All fixable but worth surfacing early.

[27:52] [30:00] Samir: Final quick recap then next steps. Recap: 1) batching at 25-40ms window for interactive chat with tuned max batch sizes; 2) prefix/KV cache with app-level normalization likely to yield 30% cost savings; 3) benchmark run to validate numbers; 4) security and BYOK supported.

[30:30] Maya: Sounds good. Quick operational Q: who at Redwood will be the day-to-day SE if we do pilot?

[30:36] Samir: Jules will be primary SE; Nina from Product will help with console config. For escalation I'm the AE.

[30:48] Tommy: Ok let's lock on dates: Maya will share the 50 prompts by Friday (2026-04-16). Pilot benchmark week of Apr 20.

[31:00] Maya: Yep we'll do that.

[31:05] [33:00] [Minor crosstalk]

[33:20] Jules: I'll also add a suggested per-route YAML config in the follow-up with the exact micro_batch_window_ms and cache rules.

[33:40] Rajiv: For contract/commit guidance — what commit levels do you typically recommend for Dedicated?

[33:46] Samir: Depends on throughput; we'll model several commit tiers in the spreadsheet. We typically see customers commit to 3-6 months after pilot if savings align.

[34:05] Maya: Any final security nuance — audit logs for cache access?

[34:11] Jules: We record access logs for cache operations and can export to your SIEM; we also provide RBAC and admin audit trails.

[34:30] [36:00] Samir: Ok time to wrap. We'll: send cost model sheet (Samir), pilot checklist (Jules), and security pack (Samir) — and schedule benchmark.

[36:20] Maya: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.

[36:30] Rajiv: Thank you.

[36:35] Samir: Appreciate it — next call tentatively Apr 23 to review readiness before pilot. I'll follow up with calendar invites.

[36:45] [End of recording — 00:52:10 according to call system]
